info.name: Tractus-X IdentityHub · Local E2E Flow (DCP)
info.description:
End-to-end DCP credential **issuance**, **presentation** and **revocation** against a locally running Tractus-X IdentityHub + IssuerService (EDC 0.17.0).

## Prerequisites
1. Build the jars and start the stack (note the two different working directories):
   - from the **repo root**: `./gradlew shadowJar`
   - from **`deployment/docker/`**: `docker compose --profile sql up -d --build`
2. Copy the two super-user API keys from the startup logs into the collection variables `IH_SUPERUSER_KEY` and `IS_SUPERUSER_KEY`:
   - `docker compose --profile sql logs identityhub | grep "API Key"`
   - `docker compose --profile sql logs issuerservice | grep "API Key"`

**That's all.** Every other variable is either a working default for the compose stack or is captured automatically by test scripts as you execute the folders in order (00 → 07). The whole collection also runs unattended in the Collection Runner or newman.

## Re-running
- A full Collection Runner / newman run **includes 99 · Cleanup**, so the stack ends without the flow's participants. To inspect state afterwards, run folders individually and skip 99.
- Wait **~10 seconds** between full runs: participants are re-created with fresh keys, and the runtimes cache resolved DID documents for 10 s — an immediate re-run fails signature checks against the stale cached keys (issuance ERROR / presentation 401).
- Holder-registry rows survive cleanup (no delete API). Re-running with the **same** variables is fine (the 409 is tolerated), but changing `HOLDER_DID` while keeping the same `HOLDER_BPN` on a used stack fails issuance — the surviving row still maps the BPN to the old DID. Reset the stack (`docker compose --profile sql down -v`) or change `HOLDER_BPN` too.

## EDC 0.17.0 gotchas encoded in this collection
- URL path segments take the **plain** `participantContextId` — base64url-encoded ids return 404 (IH #937). Only the API-key **prefix** is still base64url-encoded.
- Presentation scopes must use the Tractus-X aliases (`org.eclipse.tractusx.vc.type` / `org.eclipse.dspace.dcp.vc.type`); the upstream `org.eclipse.edc.vc.type` alias is rejected.

## Adapting to another deployment (Helm/ingress)
Change the `*_URL` collection variables to your ingress hosts, and the `*_INTERNAL_*` / `*_DID` variables to hostnames the two runtimes can reach **from inside the cluster**.

## Why the `sql` profile (or the persistence charts) is required
The issuance flow uses the `database` attestation type, which only exists in the SQL runtimes — the `*-memory` runtimes reject it with `Unknown attestation type: database`, so the flow cannot complete there.

item.name: 01 · Issuer Setup
item.description:
Creates the ParticipantContext that acts as the credential ISSUER on the IssuerService. This generates an EC P-256 keypair, publishes a did:web document with an `IssuerService` service endpoint (the address the holder's IdentityHub will call over DCP), and returns a fresh API key + STS client secret, which the scripts capture for all later requests.

item.name: 03 · Issuance Configuration (Issuer)
item.description:
Configures WHAT the issuer can issue and TO WHOM:
1. an attestation (how holder claims are verified — here: a lookup in the internal `holders` DB table),
2. a credential definition (credential type, format, validity and how attestation data maps into the credentialSubject),
3. the holder registration (populates the `holders` table the attestation reads from).

request.description: Registers the IdentityHub participant as a known holder. The row this creates is exactly what the database attestation looks up when the credential request arrives. Holder registrations survive the 99 · Cleanup folder (there is no delete API for them), so on a re-run 409 'already registered' is fine — BUT only with unchanged variables: the surviving row maps `holderId` (the BPN) to the DID it was first registered with. If you change `HOLDER_DID` and keep the same `HOLDER_BPN` on a used stack, issuance will fail against the stale mapping — reset the stack or change `HOLDER_BPN` as well.

item.name: 04 · Request Credential (DCP Issuance)
item.description:
The holder asks the issuer for a credential. One API call triggers the whole asynchronous DCP protocol:
IdentityHub resolves the issuer DID → finds the IssuerService endpoint → sends a signed CredentialRequestMessage → IssuerService verifies the token, evaluates the attestation, signs the credential and DELIVERS it back to the holder's CredentialService endpoint. Poll the status until it becomes ISSUED, then fetch the stored credential.

request.description: `holderPid` is a client-chosen correlation id for THIS request (generated fresh each run by the pre-request script); poll the status endpoint with it. The `credentials` entries must match the credential definition: same id, type and format.

item.description:
What a verifier (e.g. an EDC connector) does during the DCP presentation flow: obtain a self-issued token from the holder's STS, then query the holder's Credentials API for a Verifiable Presentation.

item.name: 06 · Credential Lifecycle (Issuer)
item.description:
Revocation management on the issuer side, backed by a BitstringStatusList credential with purpose `revocation`.

⚠️ Revocation is PERMANENT: per the W3C Bitstring Status List model only `suspension` is reversible, and this stack provisions a revocation-purpose list. `suspend` and `resume` therefore both return 501 Not Implemented here — the final request demonstrates that on purpose. Re-run folder 04 to issue a fresh credential afterwards.

item.description: Deletes the flow's participants and issuer configuration so folders 01–06 can be re-run against the same stack. Holder-registry rows, issued credentials and issuance processes have no delete API — for a fully pristine state reset the stack: `docker compose --profile sql down -v && docker compose --profile sql up -d`.
